abstract.text:
Occlusion relationship reasoning based on convolution
neural networks consists of two subtasks: occlusion boundary extraction and occlusion orientation inference. Due to
the essential differences between the two subtasks in the feature expression at the higher and lower stages, it is challenging to carry on them simultaneously in one network. To
address this issue, we propose a novel Dual-path Decoder
Network, which uniformly extracts occlusion information
at higher stages and separates into two paths to recover
boundary and occlusion orientation respectively in lower
stages. Besides, considering the restriction of occlusion orientation presentation to occlusion orientation learning, we
design a new orthogonal representation for occlusion orientation and proposed the Orthogonal Orientation Regression
loss which can get rid of the unfitness between occlusion
representation and learning and further prompt the occlusion orientation learning. Finally, we apply a multi-scale
loss together with our proposed orientation regression loss
to guide the boundary and orientation path learning respectively. Experiments demonstrate that our proposed method
achieves state-of-the-art results on PIOD and BSDS ownership datasets.

relations.quote: DOOBNet [18] designs an unified end-to-end multi-task deep object occlusion boundary detection network to simultaneously predict object boundary and occlusion orientation by sharing convolutional features.
relations.why: DOOBNet shares convolutional features for both tasks; DDNet shares only higher-stage features and separates lower-stage spatial recovery.

relations.quote: OFNet [10] considers the importance of occlusion cues for two tasks, and designs two sub-networks to share occlusion cues.
relations.why: OFNet shares occlusion cues via sub-networks; DDNet argues lower-stage decoding should be separated.

relations.quote: we use ResNet [6] as a base feature extraction model as in previous works [18, 11, 10].
relations.why: ResNet supplies the backbone feature extractor for DDNet.

relations.quote: For example, HED [20] gets multi-scale boundaries by supervising the different side-layer output results.
relations.why: DDNet adopts multi-scale supervision but applies it to decoder side outputs rather than only backbone side layers.

relations.quote: BDCN [5] performs different supervision on different side-layers to optimize side output results.
relations.why: BDCN supervises side layers directly; DDNet says previous methods lack high-level guidance for lower-stage spatial recovery.

relations.quote: Deng et al. [2] use a bottom-up/top-down architecture to predict crisp boundaries.
relations.why: The encoder-decoder idea is part of the architectural lineage DDNet builds on.

relations.quote: Based on HED [20], CED [22] implements edge enhancement by adding a decoder structure.
relations.why: CED is cited as prior decoder-based edge enhancement.

relations.quote: CEDN [21] utilizes a fully convolutional encoder-decoder network to focus on detecting higher-level object contours.
relations.why: CEDN is cited as prior fully convolutional encoder-decoder work for contours.

relations.quote: We evaluate the proposed approach on two public datasets: PIOD [19] and BSDS ownership dataset [13].
relations.why: DDNet evaluates on BSDS ownership, using it as an external benchmark.
